facts.claim: Exposure to light at night is linked to a 14% increased risk of obesity in the highest exposure group compared to the lowest.
facts.quote: A significant 14% increased risk of obesity was observed in the highest LAN exposure group compared to the lowest (OR = 1. 14, 95% CI: 1. 07-1. 22; I² = 92. 5%, P 0. 05).

facts.claim: Blue-enriched white light with a color temperature greater than 5000 Kelvin improves sleepiness in night-shift workers.
facts.quote: Further, the blue-enriched white light with a color temperature greater than 5000 Kelvin was effective in improving sleepiness of night-shift workers.

facts.claim: Light at night is linked to an increased risk of depression.
facts.quote: Our findings suggest that both outdoor and indoor ALAN exposures are associated with increased risk of depression.

facts.claim: Sleep interventions, including light therapy, improve sleep or reduce sleep disturbance among rotating night shift workers.
facts.quote: Conclusion Sleep interventions were effective in promoting sleep or reducing sleep disturbance among rotating night shift workers.

rejected.claim: Light at night is linked to an increased prevalence of bipolar disorder (OR: 1. 19; 95 % CI: 1. 08 to 1. 31) and anxiety (OR: 1. 10; 95 % CI: 1. 02 to 1. 20).
rejected.quote: LAN exposure was also associated with an increased prevalence of bipolar disorder (OR: 1. 19; 95 % CI: 1. 08 to 1. 31) and anxiety (OR: 1. 10; 95 % CI: 1. 02 to 1. 20)

rejected.claim: Light at night is linked to an increased incidence of anxiety (hazard ratio [HR]: 1. 08; 95 % CI: 1. 02 to 1. 15) and schizophrenia (HR: 1. 55; 95 % CI: 1. 01 to 2. 39).
rejected.quote: increased incidence of anxiety (hazard ratio [HR]: 1. 08; 95 % CI: 1. 02 to 1. 15) and schizophrenia (HR: 1. 55; 95 % CI: 1. 01 to 2. 39)

rejected.claim: The incidence of depression did not achieve statistical significance (HR: 1. 53; 95 % CI: 0. 98 to 2. 38) in a meta-analysis of light at night.
rejected.quote: however, the incidence of depression did not achieve statistical significance (HR: 1. 53; 95 % CI: 0. 98 to 2. 38)

research.angle: Exposure to light at night is linked to increased obesity and various mental health conditions, though its specific link to depression is not statistically significant in all analyses.
research.verdict: The evidence shows that light at night is associated with metabolic issues like obesity and several mental health disorders, while specific lighting interventions can improve sleepiness in shift workers.
research.caveat: The evidence for depression is inconsistent, with one meta-analysis failing to reach statistical significance.
